# Zendesk — Style Reference

> Olive-black ink on a linen ledger, one lime highlighter. Vanilla Sans at weight 500 for every headline, a white canvas stacked with #f5f5f2 slabs, 1px inset rings instead of shadows, and a lime fill reserved for actions.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Zendesk speaks a lime-on-ink service language. A #ffffff canvas carries #f5f5f2 linen slabs at a 40px radius, a #203524 forest vault for events, and #11110d olive-black ink for text, mockup headers and the announcement strip. Nearly every neutral tint is that same ink diluted by alpha: #11110d80 for scrims, #11110d1c for hairlines and #11110d0d for washes. The chromatic budget is one hue family. #d1f470 lime is the only filled action color, #70a32a sprout tints single words inside headlines, and the forest greens stay on dark banners and a timeline node. Vanilla Sans carries every word. Headlines from 53px to 85px use weight 500 with zero tracking, so size rather than weight builds the hierarchy. The only tracked text is a 16px weight 700 uppercase eyebrow at 0.75px. Corners sit in the rounded band: 16px buttons, 20px tiles, a 32px hero and 40px cards. Depth comes from surface shifts and 1px inset rings, not from shadows. The result reads as a consumer brand that sells software rather than a ticketing tool dressed in corporate blue.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page background, nav bar, email input fill and pause-control disc. 16 background uses and 137 text uses on dark panels — the blank sheet every slab sits on. |
| Linen Surface | `#f5f5f2` | `--color-linen-surface` | Feature cards, product cards and section slabs. It is also the 93-use type color on photography and forest — a warm off-white that keeps both surfaces and reversed text from glaring. |
| Frosted Glass | `#ffffffe6` | `--color-frosted-glass` | Single translucent layer for floating controls over the hero photo — glass appears once and stays rationed. Do not use it for cards. |
| Forest Vault | `#203524` | `--color-forest-vault` | AI Summit event banner and its countdown band, 6 uses — the only dark chromatic surface, which turns the green hue family into a full room. |
| Moss Panel | `#2d4c33` | `--color-moss-panel` | Lighter step inside the forest banner for the copy panel. 1 use — a tonal second floor rather than a new color. |
| Fog Scrim | `#11110d80` | `--color-fog-scrim` | 50% ink overlay on photography and modal backdrops, 9 uses — it darkens imagery for #f5f5f2 type without adding pure black. |
| Ink | `#11110d` | `--color-ink` | Body text, headings, nav labels, announcement strip and mockup headers. 102 text uses — an olive-tinted near-black that warms the whole grayscale. |
| Ash Border | `#d5d5d2` | `--color-ash-border` | 1px borders, the inset ring on inputs and the secondary button, and countdown tiles, 6 border uses — the main line weight of the system. |
| Mist Hairline | `#11110d1c` | `--color-mist-hairline` | 11% ink for dividers and pressed or selected tints, 7 uses — a hairline that adapts to any surface it crosses. |
| Pebble Wash | `#11110d0d` | `--color-pebble-wash` | 5% ink hover wash on menu rows and ghost buttons, 3 uses — the softest step and invisible until touched. |
| Keylime Signal | `#d1f470` | `--color-keylime-signal` | "Try for free", "Register now" and "Explore the platform" fills, 15 uses — the single filled action color. Do not use it for text on white, which falls below readable contrast. |
| Sprout Ink | `#70a32a` | `--color-sprout-ink` | Highlighted headline words ("smarter"), links and the "DIGITAL EVENT" eyebrow, 76 text uses — lime deepened until it can be read. Do not promote it to a button fill. |
| Forest Pulse | `#4e8336` | `--color-forest-pulse` | The node dot on the vertical timeline connector, 1 use — decorative punctuation. Keep it off text and buttons. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Vanilla Sans — the single grotesk that carries display, UI, eyebrow and fine print · `--font-vanilla-sans`

- **Substitute:** Inter Display at 500 for headlines and Inter at 400 or 600 for UI; Instrument Sans at 500; Plus Jakarta Sans at 500. Vanilla Sans draws slightly heavier than its nominal number, so a 500 reads close to a 520. Do not drop substitutes to 400 at display sizes, because the headlines would turn thin and editorial.
- **Weights:** 300, 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 14px, 15px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 32px, 33px, 50px, 53px, 72px, 85px
- **Line height:** 1.0 to 1.625. Display runs 1.05 to 1.15, headings 1.25, body 1.45 to 1.625.
- **Letter spacing:** 0.75px on the 16px weight 700 uppercase eyebrow, 0 on every other size including 85px display.
- **Role:** Weight 500 at 53px to 85px is the signature. Headlines are big and firm without the 700 weight that conventional SaaS heroes use. Most of the scale climbs in steps of about 1.33, close to a Perfect Fourth (53→72 is 1.36), then leaps 1.65 from 20px to 33px. Paragraphs stay compact while headings jump to a different register. Display type carries no negative tracking, which goes against the usual tight-tracked hero, so the type keeps an open, conversational spacing. The only tracking in the system belongs to the uppercase eyebrow, so labels are the one place type is set like signage.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Vanilla Sans | 400 | 14px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Vanilla Sans | 400 | 15px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body | Vanilla Sans | 600 | 16px | 1.625 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Vanilla Sans | 600 | 18px | 1.556 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Vanilla Sans | — | 20px | 1.45 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Vanilla Sans | 500 | 33px | 1.25 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Vanilla Sans | 500 | 53px | 1.15 | 0px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Vanilla Sans | 500 | 72px | 1.1 | 0px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Vanilla Sans | 500 | 85px | 1.05 | 0px | `--text-display` |

Two values outside the table also exist:

- **Eyebrow:** body size, weight 700, uppercase, 0.75px tracking (`--tracking-eyebrow`).
- **Countdown numerals:** 32px at weight 300, line height 1.0.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Reserve #d1f470 for filled action buttons and put #11110d text on it — the lime is the only filled color, and spending it elsewhere costs the call to action its pull.
- Set every headline from 33px to 85px at weight 500 with 0px tracking — size carries the hierarchy, and the medium weight keeps large type firm without shouting.
- Derive neutral tints from #11110d at alpha (#11110d1c hairlines, #11110d0d washes, #11110d80 scrims) — one olive-black ink keeps every gray warm and related.
- Use #f5f5f2 slabs at a 40px radius on #ffffff for feature storytelling — a shift of under 4% in lightness is enough to separate surfaces without lines.
- Put a 16px weight 700 uppercase eyebrow with 0.75px tracking above major headings — it is the only tracked type, so it reads as a label rather than a sentence.
- Color one or two words of a heading in #70a32a — sprout carries emphasis inside type and stays readable where lime is not.
- Separate sections with 104px of vertical space — the generous rhythm treats each slab as its own room.

### Don't

- Don't set display headlines at weight 700 with -2px tracking the way most SaaS heroes do — it swaps the system's calm weight 500 authority for generic urgency.
- Don't add a second saturated hue such as a blue CTA or a purple badge — the budget of one green family is non-negotiable, and a second hue breaks the single-highlighter thesis.
- Don't use pure #000000 or cool grays like #e5e7eb for text and borders — they clash with the olive cast of #11110d and #d5d5d2.
- Don't put #ffffff text on #d1f470 — the contrast collapses and the button stops looking like a button.
- Don't give cards drop shadows like 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.1) — elevation here is tonal, and `--shadow-md` belongs only to floating mockup bubbles.
- Don't shrink the card radius to 8px across the board — the 40px slab against the 16px button contrast is what separates places from controls.
- Don't make the navigation sticky with a blur backdrop — the static, 1px-hairlined white bar is deliberate, and #ffffffe6 glass should never leave the floating controls.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- card surface: #f5f5f2 (Linen Surface)
- primary text: #11110d (Ink)
- border: #d5d5d2 (Ash Border)
- inverted surface: #203524 (Forest Vault)
- text accent: #70a32a (Sprout Ink)
- primary action: #d1f470 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts use #11110d and alpha steps of it (#11110d1c, #11110d80) as the structural series, #70a32a as the single highlighted series, and #d1f470 only as a background band behind the key value — lime is never the boldest bar.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button. Use a #d1f470 background, #11110d text, no border, a 16px border-radius and 10px 16px padding. Set Vanilla Sans (fallback Inter) at 16px weight 600 with a 1.625 line height and no shadow. Make a large variant at 18px weight 600 with 10px 20px padding and a 48px height. On hover, overlay a #11110d0d wash. Place it beside a ghost twin with a transparent background, #11110d text, the same radius and padding, and an `inset 0 0 0 1px #d5d5d2` ring, with 8px between them.

2. Build a hero section. Use a #ffffff page with 16px side margins and a rounded image slab at a 32px radius containing a warm portrait photo under a #11110d80 overlay. Left-align the content with 120px left padding. The order: an eyebrow at 16px weight 700 uppercase, 0.75px tracking, #f5f5f2; then a 24px gap and an 85px weight 500 headline at 1.05 line height, 0px tracking, #f5f5f2; then a 20px weight 400 subline in #ffffff at a 1.45 line height; then a 15px trust line. Below them, put a 48px-tall #ffffff email input with a 12px radius, 12px padding and an `inset 0 0 0 1px #d5d5d2` ring, and the 48px lime button 16px to its right. Float a #ffffff receipt card with a 20px radius and `0 20px 30px 0 rgba(23, 73, 77, 0.15)` at the bottom right.

3. Build a feature card. Use a #f5f5f2 background, a 40px border-radius, 32px padding and no border or shadow, at full container width and about 240px tall. Put a 33px weight 500 #11110d heading at a 1.25 line height in the top left, wrapped to two lines within 542px. On the right, stack two #ffffff chat bubbles with a 16px radius, 12px padding, 14px weight 400 #11110d text and `0 8px 24px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)`, with 8px between them. Connect stacked cards with a 1px #11110d1c vertical line and 104px of vertical spacing.

4. Build a navigation bar. Use a static, full-width #ffffff bar with a 1px #d5d5d2 bottom border and an inner max-width of 1600px. The top utility row holds right-aligned 14px weight 400 #11110d links with 16px line icons and 24px gaps. In the main row, put the logo on the left, centered menu triggers at 16px weight 600 #11110d with chevrons 4px apart and 32px gaps, and on the right the lime primary button and the ghost button (both 16px radius, 10px 16px padding) with 8px between them.

5. Build an event banner. Use a 40px-radius container split into a #2d4c33 left panel with 32px padding and a #203524 bottom band. Set a 53px weight 500 #f5f5f2 title, 16px weight 400 #f5f5f2 copy, a #70a32a eyebrow at 16px weight 700 uppercase with 0.75px tracking, and the lime Register button. Add three countdown tiles with 1px #d5d5d2 borders, an 8px radius and 32px weight 300 #f5f5f2 numerals. Fill the right half with two speaker photos with no border.

## Components

### Pill-Soft Button — Keylime (Primary)

**Role:** The single filled call to action

A lime tablet with ink text. The spec is a #d1f470 background, #11110d text, no border, a 16px radius and 10px 16px padding. It uses Vanilla Sans at 16px weight 600 with no shadow. The large form in the hero and the event banner steps up to 18px weight 600, 10px 20px padding and a 48px height. Ink rather than white sits on the lime because lime cannot hold white type. This is the only filled chromatic element on the page, so use it once per viewport for the conversion step.

### Outline Button — Ghost (Secondary)

**Role:** Demo and secondary navigation actions

An outlined companion at the same size. The spec is a transparent background on #ffffff, #11110d text, a 1px inset #d5d5d2 ring (estimated from the screenshot, matching the measured input ring), a 16px radius and 10px 16px padding. It uses Vanilla Sans at 16px weight 600 with no shadow, and hover fills with #11110d0d. It matches the primary in every dimension, so the pair reads as two choices of equal size and different loudness. Lime stays the only one with mass.

### Navigation Bar — Two-Tier White

**Role:** Global wayfinding and conversion entry

A static two-tier header. A #ffffff bar carries a top utility row of 14px weight 400 #11110d links with line icons (Sign in, Contact us, Language). Below it sits the main row: the logo on the left, centered menu triggers in Vanilla Sans at 16px weight 600 with chevrons, and the lime and ghost buttons on the right with an 8px gap. A 1px #d5d5d2 hairline closes the bar, and link focus radii are 4px. The bar does not stick, which is anti-convention for SaaS and shows the page trusts the hero to sell before the menu does.

### Announcement Strip — Ink Band

**Role:** Event promotion above everything

A full-width ink ribbon. The spec is a #11110d background with #ffffff 14px weight 400 text, an inline "Register now" link at 14px weight 600, and a close icon pinned right, all on a 4px link radius. It is the only full-bleed ink band on the page, so it sits above the nav like a printed tab and makes the white header below feel lighter.

### Hero — Photographic Slab

**Role:** Headline, proof claim and email capture

A rounded photograph inset from the page edges. The panel carries a 32px radius with left-aligned type over a warm portrait darkened by #11110d80. The order: a #f5f5f2 eyebrow at 16px weight 700 uppercase with 0.75px tracking, an 85px weight 500 display headline at 1.05 line height, a 20px weight 400 subline, and a 15px trust note. Below them, an email input and the large lime button sit 16px apart. A floating #ffffff receipt mockup at a 20px radius anchors the bottom right. Use the slab once, at the top.

### Email Capture Input

**Role:** Inline trial signup field

A quiet white field. The spec is a #ffffff background, #11110d text, no border, the 1px inset #d5d5d2 ring (`--shadow-subtle`), a 12px radius, 12px padding and a 48px height. It uses Vanilla Sans at 15px weight 400. The 12px radius sits one step inside the 16px button beside it, so field and button read as related parts rather than twins.

### Logo Strip — Customer Proof

**Role:** Social proof beneath the hero

A single row of monochrome logos. A two-line #11110d eyebrow ("22,000+ service teams trust Zendesk AI") at 16px weight 700 uppercase with 0.75px tracking sits on the left. Eight wordmarks in #11110d spread evenly across the remaining width on #ffffff, with 104px of space above and below. There are no cards, borders or color, so the logos act as typography in the ink rather than a sticker wall.

### Event Banner — Forest Vault (Outlier)

**Role:** Time-bound event promotion

The system outlier, a dark green room. A 40px-radius container splits into a #2d4c33 copy panel and a #203524 countdown band, with a speaker photo grid on the right. Inside are #f5f5f2 type at 53px weight 500 for the title, 16px body, a #70a32a uppercase eyebrow, and the lime button. Countdown tiles use 1px #d5d5d2 borders (estimated), an 8px radius and 32px weight 300 numerals. It breaks the light canvas on purpose, because events need urgency the neutral slabs cannot carry.

### Feature Card — Linen Slab

**Role:** Platform capability storytelling

The workhorse surface, a large warm slab. The spec is a #f5f5f2 background, #11110d text, no border, a 40px radius and 32px padding, with no shadow on the slab. A 33px weight 500 heading at 1.25 sits in the top left, and a product mockup floats on the right. Chat bubbles inside the mockup are #ffffff at a 16px radius with `--shadow-md`, the only place a real shadow appears. Use it for one idea per card, stacked vertically.

### Timeline Connector

**Role:** Links stacked feature slabs

A 1px vertical #11110d1c line runs between feature slabs. It starts from an 8px-radius #4e8336 node dot under the "Explore the platform" button. It is punctuation rather than decoration: it turns a stack of identical cards into a sequence and replaces arrows or step numbers.

### Product Card — Featured

**Role:** Product tier entry point

A compact linen tile. The spec is a #f5f5f2 background, #11110d text, a 1px border, a 16px radius, a clipped top image and 32px 24px padding in the text block. It opens with an uppercase eyebrow at 16px weight 700 with 0.75px tracking, then a 20px weight 600 title. A "Learn more" link closes it at 16px weight 600, with an 8px gap above. The 16px radius matches the buttons, so the small cards read as clickable while the 40px slabs read as places.

### Floating Circle Controls

**Role:** Chat launcher and media pause

Two circular controls. The chat launcher is a #11110d disc with a #ffffff icon. The pause control is a #ffffff disc at the hero's bottom right. Both use a 100% radius, sit at about 40px (snapped from a measured 42px) and have no shadow. These are the only circles in the system, which marks them as tools that hover over content.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Reserve #d1f470 for filled action buttons and put #11110d text on it — the lime is the only filled color, and spending it elsewhere costs the call to action its pull.
- Set every headline from 33px to 85px at weight 500 with 0px tracking — size carries the hierarchy, and the medium weight keeps large type firm without shouting.
- Derive neutral tints from #11110d at alpha (#11110d1c hairlines, #11110d0d washes, #11110d80 scrims) — one olive-black ink keeps every gray warm and related.
- Use #f5f5f2 slabs at a 40px radius on #ffffff for feature storytelling — a shift of under 4% in lightness is enough to separate surfaces without lines.
- Put a 16px weight 700 uppercase eyebrow with 0.75px tracking above major headings — it is the only tracked type, so it reads as a label rather than a sentence.
- Color one or two words of a heading in #70a32a — sprout carries emphasis inside type and stays readable where lime is not.
- Separate sections with 104px of vertical space — the generous rhythm treats each slab as its own room.

### Don't

- Don't set display headlines at weight 700 with -2px tracking the way most SaaS heroes do — it swaps the system's calm weight 500 authority for generic urgency.
- Don't add a second saturated hue such as a blue CTA or a purple badge — the budget of one green family is non-negotiable, and a second hue breaks the single-highlighter thesis.
- Don't use pure #000000 or cool grays like #e5e7eb for text and borders — they clash with the olive cast of #11110d and #d5d5d2.
- Don't put #ffffff text on #d1f470 — the contrast collapses and the button stops looking like a button.
- Don't give cards drop shadows like 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.1) — elevation here is tonal, and `--shadow-md` belongs only to floating mockup bubbles.
- Don't shrink the card radius to 8px across the board — the 40px slab against the 16px button contrast is what separates places from controls.
- Don't make the navigation sticky with a blur backdrop — the static, 1px-hairlined white bar is deliberate, and #ffffffe6 glass should never leave the floating controls.

## Surfaces

| Level | Name | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | Page background, nav, logo strip and the whitespace between slabs |
| 1 | Linen Surface | `#f5f5f2` | Feature slabs and product cards, the main content tier |
| 2 | Frosted Glass | `#ffffffe6` | Floating controls over hero photography |
| 3 | Forest Vault | `#203524` | Event banner, the single dark chromatic room |
| 4 | Ink | `#11110d` | Announcement strip, chat launcher and mockup header bars |

## Elevation

- **Inputs and secondary buttons:** `inset 0 0 0 1px #d5d5d2`
- **Tab and segmented underlines:** `inset 0 2px 0 0 #d5d5d2`
- **Floating chat bubbles inside feature mockups:** `0 8px 24px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)`
- **Floating receipt and dashboard mockups over photography:** `0 20px 30px 0 rgba(23, 73, 77, 0.15)`

Four shadows across a 34-section page, each used once, shows that cast shadow is the exception. Structural surfaces rely on the #ffffff to #f5f5f2 tonal step and on 1px inset rings. Real shadows are confined to product mockups that need to float above a photo or slab.

## Imagery

The home page pairs warm, cinematic lifestyle photography with stylized product mockups, and it has no illustration system. The hero is a full-bleed portrait in amber tones, with a green headphone that echoes the lime. It is cropped into a 32px-radius slab and darkened by a #11110d80 scrim so #f5f5f2 type holds. Speaker portraits in the event banner sit on decorative pixel-grid backdrops in blue and violet. These are campaign art, not system tokens. Product UI appears as simplified white cards at 16px to 20px radii with `--shadow-md` or `--shadow-lg`, floated over #f5f5f2 slabs. Blue buttons inside the "Fill knowledge gaps" mockup are mockup-internal. Icons are 1.5px line glyphs in #11110d at nav size. There are no gradients, glows or orbs. The images tell the story of a calm human helped by AI that works quietly in the background.

## Layout

Content sits inside a 1600px container, with readable columns narrowing to 1080px, 700px and 542px. Sections follow a 104px rhythm. The hero is a single inset photo slab with type on the left, image interest on the right and email capture under the headline. Below it come a one-row logo strip with an eight-logo grid, a full-width forest event banner, a centered 53px heading with a lime button, and a vertical chain of 40px-radius #f5f5f2 feature slabs linked by a 1px timeline line. Product cards then sit in a three-column row. The nav is static and white, about 72px tall, with the logo left, menus centered and buttons right, plus a 14px utility row above. The footer is a tall multi-column link grid. At 375px, use the 53px heading size for the hero display and 64px section gaps. Overall density: spacious.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- card surface: #f5f5f2 (Linen Surface)
- primary text: #11110d (Ink)
- border: #d5d5d2 (Ash Border)
- inverted surface: #203524 (Forest Vault)
- text accent: #70a32a (Sprout Ink)
- primary action: #d1f470 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts use #11110d and alpha steps of it (#11110d1c, #11110d80) as the structural series, #70a32a as the single highlighted series, and #d1f470 only as a background band behind the key value — lime is never the boldest bar.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button. Use a #d1f470 background, #11110d text, no border, a 16px border-radius and 10px 16px padding. Set Vanilla Sans (fallback Inter) at 16px weight 600 with a 1.625 line height and no shadow. Make a large variant at 18px weight 600 with 10px 20px padding and a 48px height. On hover, overlay a #11110d0d wash. Place it beside a ghost twin with a transparent background, #11110d text, the same radius and padding, and an `inset 0 0 0 1px #d5d5d2` ring, with 8px between them.

2. Build a hero section. Use a #ffffff page with 16px side margins and a rounded image slab at a 32px radius containing a warm portrait photo under a #11110d80 overlay. Left-align the content with 120px left padding. The order: an eyebrow at 16px weight 700 uppercase, 0.75px tracking, #f5f5f2; then a 24px gap and an 85px weight 500 headline at 1.05 line height, 0px tracking, #f5f5f2; then a 20px weight 400 subline in #ffffff at a 1.45 line height; then a 15px trust line. Below them, put a 48px-tall #ffffff email input with a 12px radius, 12px padding and an `inset 0 0 0 1px #d5d5d2` ring, and the 48px lime button 16px to its right. Float a #ffffff receipt card with a 20px radius and `0 20px 30px 0 rgba(23, 73, 77, 0.15)` at the bottom right.

3. Build a feature card. Use a #f5f5f2 background, a 40px border-radius, 32px padding and no border or shadow, at full container width and about 240px tall. Put a 33px weight 500 #11110d heading at a 1.25 line height in the top left, wrapped to two lines within 542px. On the right, stack two #ffffff chat bubbles with a 16px radius, 12px padding, 14px weight 400 #11110d text and `0 8px 24px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)`, with 8px between them. Connect stacked cards with a 1px #11110d1c vertical line and 104px of vertical spacing.

4. Build a navigation bar. Use a static, full-width #ffffff bar with a 1px #d5d5d2 bottom border and an inner max-width of 1600px. The top utility row holds right-aligned 14px weight 400 #11110d links with 16px line icons and 24px gaps. In the main row, put the logo on the left, centered menu triggers at 16px weight 600 #11110d with chevrons 4px apart and 32px gaps, and on the right the lime primary button and the ghost button (both 16px radius, 10px 16px padding) with 8px between them.

5. Build an event banner. Use a 40px-radius container split into a #2d4c33 left panel with 32px padding and a #203524 bottom band. Set a 53px weight 500 #f5f5f2 title, 16px weight 400 #f5f5f2 copy, a #70a32a eyebrow at 16px weight 700 uppercase with 0.75px tracking, and the lime Register button. Add three countdown tiles with 1px #d5d5d2 borders, an 8px radius and 32px weight 300 #f5f5f2 numerals. Fill the right half with two speaker photos with no border.

## Alpha Ink Discipline

The neutral system is one pigment, #11110d, diluted to set strengths: 5% wash (#11110d0d), 11% hairline (#11110d1c) and 50% scrim (#11110d80). The only opaque grays are #d5d5d2 and #f5f5f2, both tinted toward the same olive. This is why the page feels warm without any beige surface. What would break it is a Tailwind default gray such as #6b7280 for captions, or a pure black overlay. Either one adds a cool second pigment, and the warmth turns into clutter. To extend the system, mix any new state (disabled, selected, divider on dark) as #11110d at a new alpha. On forest, use #f5f5f2 at alpha instead. A new opaque gray should be the exception and must lean olive.

## Single Highlighter Budget

Saturated color is one green family with a strict division of labor. #d1f470 fills buttons, #70a32a colors words, #4e8336 marks a node, and #203524 builds one dark room. Lime appears on roughly 15 elements across 34 sections, so it reads as a highlighter stroke rather than a theme. Common mistakes break this: tinting a card #d1f470 at 20%, making lime icons, or adding a blue "new" badge. Each one teaches the eye that lime is decoration, and the next button loses its pull. To extend, give new emphasis to type first through weight, size or a sprout word. Bring in forest only when a section needs urgency. Photography and mockup internals may carry other hues, but they never become tokens.

## Medium-Weight Authority

Headlines run weight 500 at every display size: 85px, 72px, 53px and 33px. Tracking stays at 0px, where convention would push 700 and negative letter-spacing. The authority comes from scale and whitespace, as in a magazine cover. A quiet weight leaves room for the lime to be the loudest object. Raising headings to 700 would break this, because the type would compete with the button. So would tightening tracking to -2px, which would turn the open, approachable voice into startup urgency. To extend, add new levels on the existing steps of about 1.33, and keep weight 600 for 16px to 20px UI labels and 700 for uppercase eyebrows only.

## Similar Brands

- **Wise** — uses a bright lime fill on forest-green and ink neutrals as its single action color. Wise uses lime more widely on surfaces, while Zendesk keeps it to buttons.
- **Intercom** — the closest category competitor, with ink-led customer-service marketing, large medium-weight headlines and product mockups floated over neutral slabs instead of illustration.
- **Robinhood** — keeps an electric yellow-green as the rationed highlight against near-black ink. Robinhood leans dark-canvas where Zendesk stays on #ffffff.
- **Freshworks** — a direct competitor with the same rounded-slab feature storytelling, but its multi-hue palette breaks the single-family discipline Zendesk keeps.
- **Klarna** — runs a single-accent fill (pink) with soft rounded cards and warm lifestyle photography, the same consumer-grade warmth applied to a B2B story.
